committee: CC Commission for Persons with Disabilities
overview: The Commission for Persons with Disabilities advocates for the equal status of disabled residents in Medford's political and social spheres. The body advises on city infrastructure projects, monitors compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, and coordinates public resources. Meeting records from 2024 through 2026 show a focus on improving physical accessibility at City Hall, transit stations, and polling locations. As of the most recent meeting, the commission is prioritizing city intersections for accessible pedestrian signal upgrades and reviewing city-wide transition plans.

threads.name: Annual Disability Fair
threads.summary: The commission organizes an annual fair to provide resources and community engagement for disabled residents. Planning for the 2024 and 2025 events involved selecting sites like the McGlynn school and inclusive playgrounds to ensure accessibility for all attendees. While the 2025 fair was held in May, the commission began evaluating whether to move future iterations to the fall to avoid city scheduling conflicts. In recent recaps, members noted successes in community attendance while identifying a need for improved signage and water availability.

threads.name: City Hall and Public Infrastructure Upgrades
threads.summary: The commission oversees the installation of assistive technology and physical improvements in municipal buildings. This work has included procuring new cushioned armchairs and assistive listening receivers for the City Hall chambers. Recent progress includes the completed installation of an accessible ramp at the McGlynn School and ongoing design work for fully accessible public bathrooms. The commission is also involved in a city-wide self-evaluation and transition plan conducted by the Institute for Human-Centered Design.

threads.name: Transit and Transportation Advocacy
threads.summary: Advocacy for accessible transit has centered on major rail and bus improvements. The commission monitored progress on the West Medford commuter rail station, including wayfinding signage updates and the 2025 opening of a new accessible ramp. Traffic Director Todd Blake has also collaborated with the body to address MBTA bus route changes and pedestrian safety concerns. Members continue to report and review community complaints regarding sidewalk obstructions and 'The Ride' transit services.

threads.name: Pedestrian Signal and Curb Cut Improvements
threads.summary: Improving safe navigation for pedestrians is a primary focus for the commission. Early efforts included supporting municipal grant applications for curb cuts near the high school and other high-traffic public locations. This work evolved into a collaboration with the Traffic and Transportation department to install accessible pedestrian signal buttons at key intersections. By late 2026, the commission was actively prioritizing a list of candidate intersections for upgrades funded by a casino mitigation grant.

threads.name: Election and Polling Place Accessibility
threads.summary: To ensure equal participation in the political sphere, the commission coordinates with the Elections Commission on polling site readiness. Early discussions focused on the proper setup of accessible voting machines and the training of poll workers to assist disabled voters. The body has reviewed statements from the elections department regarding machine calibration and conducted its own site visits to verify equipment accessibility. These efforts are part of a broader mandate to ensure accessibility during municipal and federal elections.

threads.name: Park and Recreation Accessibility
threads.summary: The commission provides feedback on the redesign and maintenance of Medford's public parks to ensure they are inclusive. This includes reviewing plans for Carr Park, the McGlynn school play space, and the redesign of Tufts Park. For the Tufts Park project, commissioners provided specific feedback regarding accessible pathways, restroom accessibility, and screen reader compatibility for design surveys. The body also contributes to the city's Open Space and Recreation Plan by identifying barriers to park access.

threads.name: Digital Resource and Website Management
threads.summary: The commission manages a list of disability resources on the city's website, which it periodically audits for accuracy and relevance. Initial work involved restructuring the resource list into accordions to improve user experience. Recent efforts include monitoring the accessibility of digital communications sent by city consultants. The commission also uses these platforms to promote programs like the SMART 911 emergency registration system and transportation services.
